title: Hol vagy? A városban
titleEn: In town: -ban/-ben and the a→á, e→é rule
summary: Shops, school, hospital: most places in town take -ban/-ben. Final a and e get longer, and compounds follow their last part.

sections.text: For most buildings and rooms, *in* is **-ban** (back and most mixed words) or **-ben** (front words). The same vowel harmony you already know decides which.
**Final a → á, final e → é** before ANY ending, not just -ban/-ben: alma → alm**á**t, iskola → iskol**á**ba, iroda → irod**á**ban; lecke → leck**é**t, zene → zen**é**ben.

A compound is two words glued together. **Ignore the first part** and apply vowel harmony to the **last** one: (Buda)**pest** → Budapest**en**, (konyha)**szekrény** → konyhaszekrény**ben**, (számító)**gép** → számítógép**ben**, (könyv)**tár** → könyvtár**ban**.

A few places use **-n / -on / -en / -ön** (“on”) instead of -ban/-ben. Learn them one by one: a post**á**n (at the post office), a piac**on** (at the market), az egyetem**en** (at university), a pályaudvar**on** (at the railway station).
For new international words, look at the **last syllable**: hot**el** → hotel**ben**, fot**el** → fotel**ben**, but tax**i** → taxi**ban**, kávé → kávé**ban**.

A few places use **-n / -on / -en / -ön** ("on") instead of -ban/-ben. Learn them as you meet them: a posta**n**? no: a post**á**n (post office), a piac**on** (market), az egyetem**en** (university), a pályaudvar**on** (railway station).

items.en: The doctor works in the hospital.
The waiter is in the restaurant.
Where are you? — I'm at the bakery.
